## Structure and components

- [statement] ACTEGA warns that excessive coating slows drying. Adding a thicker layer is therefore not an unconditional remedy for blocking. (low confidence) — https://www.actega.com/emea/en/services/troubleshooting/blocking-printed-sheets.html · keywords: Playing-card coating application curing and compatibility, In-house playing-card coating application and curing

## How it works

- [statement] ACTEGA treats IR/hot-air dryer settings as application-specific and advises sufficient exhaust air and reduced pile pressure when troubleshooting blocking. These are separate process controls, not a universal cure recipe. (low confidence) — https://www.actega.com/emea/en/services/troubleshooting/blocking-printed-sheets.html · keywords: Playing-card coating application curing and compatibility, In-house playing-card coating application and curing
- [statement] Star Laminators requires dry inks without paraffin waxes, silicones or other slip additives for its UV-coating process. Chicago Laminating also identifies wax/Teflon and incompletely dried ink as adhesion risks. Qualify the actual printed sheet before adopting an offline UV step. (medium confidence) — https://starlaminators.com/products-services/uv-coating/ · keywords: Playing-card coating application curing and compatibility, In-house playing-card coating application and curing · also: https://www.chicagolam.com/faqs/
- [statement] Duplo requires compatibility testing for all substrates in its application-testing process. EzraCard separately recommends testing a sample for surface friction and shuffle feel. Use both compatibility and handling acceptance for the intended printed-card construction. (medium confidence) — https://app.duplousa.com/contact/atr.aspx · keywords: Playing-card coating application curing and compatibility, In-house playing-card coating application and curing · also: https://ezracard.com/finishing-options/uv-coating/
- [statement] For its Micro coater, Graphic Whizard documents lamp and reflector cleaning when coating smears, and impression-roller and scraper-blade cleaning when coating appears on sheet backs. It separately specifies a tape-pull check for adhesion complaints. Include these diagnosis and maintenance activities when evaluating the coating workflow. (low confidence) — https://www.graphicwhizard.com/faq/ · keywords: Playing-card coating application curing and compatibility, In-house playing-card coating application and curing
- [statement] Cork advises washing and drying the aqueous coater blanket or plate when a press stoppage exceeds one minute. This supplier instruction identifies an interruption-related operator task; it does not measure labor for a small card batch. (low confidence) — https://corkindustries.net/aqueous-and-uv-coatings-tricks-to-cleanup-process/ · keywords: Playing-card coating application curing and compatibility, In-house playing-card coating application and curing
- [statement] American Ultraviolet identifies bulb and reflector-liner upkeep as regular maintenance for UV curing systems. Include curing-system maintenance when assessing ownership. (low confidence) — https://www.americanultraviolet.com/uv-curing-solutions/faq-curing.cfml · keywords: Playing-card coating application curing and compatibility, In-house playing-card coating application and curing
- [statement] American Ultraviolet presents tape adhesion and scratch testing as common checks for cure completeness. Cork qualifies this advice: tape tests reveal little about cure, and its listed shop tests do not establish absolute cure. Treat these as attributed test limitations when defining sample acceptance. (medium confidence) — https://www.americanultraviolet.com/uv-curing-solutions/faq-curing.cfml · keywords: Playing-card coating application curing and compatibility, In-house playing-card coating application and curing · also: https://corkindustries.net/testing-the-cure-of-electron-beam-eb-and-ultraviolet-uv-coatings/

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] PrintPlanet contributor hondarr9 reports that an added UV lamp did not improve coating results on their KM output. This historical operator account shows why added lamp power alone cannot be assumed to solve an unqualified ink/coating combination; it is not a current printer-brand compatibility verdict. (low confidence) — https://printplanet.com/threads/uv-coating-over-digital.14279/ · keywords: Playing-card coating application curing and compatibility, In-house playing-card coating application and curing

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] DPS reports supplier guidance that wet versus dry toner dictates coating selection, and that dye, pigment, UV and solvent inkjet systems may need different coatings. A generic digital-print label is insufficient to select a formulation. (low confidence) — https://dpsmagazine.com/coating-choices/ · keywords: Playing-card coating application curing and compatibility, In-house playing-card coating application and curing

This is a specific compatibility counterexample, not proof that every inkjet print needs the same treatment.
